title = "The left contraction is the metric projection"

The left contraction is the grade-lowering part of the
[[b65e7fa9|geometric product]]. For multivectors $A$ and $B$, with
$A_r$ the grade-$r$ part of $A$ and $B_s$ the grade-$s$ part of $B$,

```typst
A dot B = sum_(r,s) (A_r B_s)_(s-r), quad s >= r,
```

where $(A_r B_s)_(s-r)$ means "keep only the grade-$(s-r)$ part". On vectors it
is the ordinary dot product, so it carries the metric. On a vector and a
bivector it does something more useful than a number: for the basis vectors
$e_1$ and $e_2$,

```typst
e_1 dot (e_1 and e_2) = e_2, quad
e_2 dot (e_1 and e_2) = -e_1.
```

Contracting with $e_1$ projects onto the plane and rotates by a quarter turn
inside it. That is the geometric content of "multiply by $i$" in complex
numbers, promoted to any dimension.

```ocaml
open Geom

E3.to_array (E3.inner E3.e1 (E3.op E3.e1 E3.e2))  (* e2 *)
E3.to_array (E3.inner E3.e2 (E3.op E3.e1 E3.e2))  (* -e1 *)
E3.to_array (E3.inner E3.e3 (E3.op E3.e1 E3.e2))  (* zero: orthogonal *)
```

The contraction is what makes incidence a scalar equation in the conformal
model. A point $X$ lies on a sphere $S$, a plane $pi$, a line $ell$ or a
circle $z$ exactly when $X dot O = 0$, where $O$ is the object blade in the
[[decc193a|working representation]] ([[b24b87b3|Distance is an inner product]],
[[86c369c2|Round versus flat: the e∞ contraction decides]]). It is also the natural way to extract the geometric content of
an object blade: $e_oo dot z$ for a circle $z$ is its carrier plane
([[44386f9a|The carrier plane of a circle]]), where $e_oo$ is the point at infinity
([[eb4daacf|e∞ is the point at infinity]]).

<figcaption style="text-align:center;font-size:0.85em;opacity:0.7;margin-top:0.4em">The contraction is a quarter turn in the plane: contracting e1 with the plane e12 gives e2, and contracting e2 with it gives -e1.</figcaption>
</figure>

The library calls it `inner`, and `scalar_prod` is its grade-zero companion.
